salmanshh_simple_spring.name: Simple Spring
salmanshh_simple_spring.description: Simple numeric spring physics with multiple named springs per behavior instance, plus object-level mesh effects.

stiffness.name: Default Stiffness
stiffness.desc: Default stiffness applied to newly created springs. How quickly the spring responds - increase for faster response.

damping.name: Default Damping
damping.desc: Default damping applied to newly created springs (0-1). Increase to reduce overshoot and oscillation.

precision.name: Default Precision
precision.desc: Default precision applied to newly created springs. Threshold to consider animation complete - lower values require closer proximity to target.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.desc: Enable or disable the spring behavior.

ConstantColour.display-text: Constant Spring "{0}" property Colour to ({2}, {3}, {4}) in {1}, (Apply to Property: {5})
ConstantColour.description: Enable or update a constant colour spring, springing toward the given target each tick. New springs inherit the behavior's default stiffness, damping, and precision. Use the Settings ACE to override per spring. Use Pause/Stop playback ACEs to deactivate.

springId.name: Spring ID
springId.desc: Unique id for the colour spring.

colourSpace.name: Colour Space
colourSpace.desc: How to interpret the channel values.

to3.name: Target Channel 3
to3.desc: RGB: Blue, HSL: Lightness, HSV: Value.

applyToProperties.name: Apply To Properties
applyToProperties.desc: Apply the sprung colour to the instance properties.

SetColourSpringSettings.display-text: Set colour spring "{0}" settings to stiffness {1}, damping {2}, precision {3}
SetColourSpringSettings.description: Set stiffness, damping, and precision for all three channels of a named colour spring.

springId.name: Spring ID
springId.desc: Unique id for the colour spring.

SetColourSpringSettingsFromDuration.list-name: Settings: Set colour spring from duration
SetColourSpringSettingsFromDuration.display-text: Set colour spring "{0}" settings from duration {1}s, precision {2}, bounce profile {3}
SetColourSpringSettingsFromDuration.description: Compute stiffness and damping so a colour spring settles in about the requested duration, with a selectable bounce profile.

springId.name: Spring ID
springId.desc: Unique id for the colour spring.

duration.name: Duration
duration.desc: Approximate time in seconds for the spring to settle.

bounceProfile.name: Bounce Profile
bounceProfile.desc: How bouncy the duration fit should be.

SpringColour.display-text: Spring colour "{0}" ({2}) from ({3}, {4}, {5}) to ({6}, {7}, {8}) in {1}, Apply to Property ({9})
SpringColour.description: Combined colour spring action for current-to-target or from-to workflows with optional apply-to-properties.

springId.name: Spring ID
springId.desc: Unique id for the colour spring.

colourSpace.name: Colour Space
colourSpace.desc: How to interpret the channel values.

startMode.name: Start Mode
startMode.desc: Current value uses the spring's current value. From value uses explicit from channels.

from1.name: From Channel 1
from1.desc: Used when Start Mode is From value. RGB: Red, HSL/HSV: Hue.

from2.name: From Channel 2
from2.desc: Used when Start Mode is From value. RGB: Green, HSL/HSV: Saturation.

from3.name: From Channel 3
from3.desc: Used when Start Mode is From value. RGB: Blue, HSL: Lightness, HSV: Value.

to3.name: To Channel 3
to3.desc: RGB: Blue, HSL: Lightness, HSV: Value.

applyToProperties.name: Apply To Properties
applyToProperties.desc: Apply the sprung colour to the instance properties.

MeshConstantSway.display-text: Start constant sway angle {0}, strength {1}, wavelength {2}, speed {3}, auto mesh {4}
MeshConstantSway.description: Start continuous sinusoidal sway. The mesh keeps swaying automatically each tick until Stop Constant Sway is called. Great for grass, plants, cloth, or flags.

angle.name: Angle
angle.desc: Direction the wave travels in degrees. 0 = rightward (vertical swaying bands, ideal for grass). 90 = downward (horizontal bands, useful for hanging cloth).

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: Peak displacement per sway crest. 0.05 is very subtle rustle, 0.1 is natural breeze, 0.2+ is strong wind.

wavelength.name: Wavelength
wavelength.desc: Spacing between sway peaks in normalized units. 0.5 gives two peaks across the sprite; 1.0 gives one broad S-curve.

speed.name: Speed
speed.desc: Oscillation speed in cycles per second. 0.5 is slow/lazy, 1.0 is natural breeze, 2.0+ is stormy flutter.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a mesh if none exists. No: skip if no mesh exists.

MeshDirectionalBend.display-text: Directional bend angle {0}, strength {1}, radius {2}, falloff {3}, auto mesh {4}
MeshDirectionalBend.description: Bend the mesh toward a direction with stronger motion on the leading edge. Great for wind push, recoil lean, and directional impact anticipation.

angle.name: Angle
angle.desc: Direction to bend toward in degrees. 0 = right, 90 = down, 180 = left, -90 = up.

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: Bend intensity. 0.08 is subtle lean, 0.2 is strong directional push, 0.35+ is exaggerated cartoon bend.

radius.name: Radius
radius.desc: How wide the bend influence is from center. 1.0 affects almost the whole sprite, 0.5 keeps bend more central.

falloff.name: Falloff
falloff.desc: Linear: even fade. Smooth: softer edges. Exponential: concentrated center influence.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5x5 mesh grid if none exists. No: skip if no mesh grid exists.

MeshImpactTrailWave.list-name: Do Mesh Effect: Impact trail wave
MeshImpactTrailWave.display-text: Impact trail wave at ({0}, {1}) angle {2}, strength {3}, wavelength {4}, trail width {5}, auto mesh {6}
MeshImpactTrailWave.description: Create a directional banded wave from an impact path. Ideal for slash trails, dash wake distortion, and projectile fly-by pressure waves.

centerX.name: Origin X
centerX.desc: Horizontal origin of the trail wave in normalized sprite space.

centerY.name: Origin Y
centerY.desc: Vertical origin of the trail wave in normalized sprite space.

angle.name: Angle
angle.desc: Direction the trail wave travels in degrees. Match to attack or dash direction.

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: Wave displacement intensity. 0.08 subtle, 0.2 dramatic, 0.35+ extreme.

wavelength.name: Wavelength
wavelength.desc: Spacing between alternating bands. Smaller values create tighter stripes.

trailWidth.name: Trail Width
trailWidth.desc: Width of the impact corridor around the travel axis. Smaller is tighter slash line; larger is broad shock path.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5x5 mesh grid if none exists. No: skip if no mesh grid exists.

MeshNoiseJitterBurst.list-name: Do Mesh Effect: Noise jitter burst
MeshNoiseJitterBurst.display-text: Noise jitter burst at ({0}, {1}) strength {2}, radius {3}, falloff {4}, auto mesh {5}
MeshNoiseJitterBurst.description: Apply randomized per-vertex impulse for electric shock, glitch hit, fear tremor, or explosion rattle, then spring back naturally.

centerX.name: Center X
centerX.desc: Horizontal burst origin in normalized sprite space (0=left, 0.5=center, 1=right).

centerY.name: Center Y
centerY.desc: Vertical burst origin in normalized sprite space (0=top, 0.5=center, 1=bottom).

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: Jitter intensity. 0.05 is subtle shake, 0.15 is strong tremor, 0.3+ is violent burst.

radius.name: Radius
radius.desc: Area of effect from burst center. 1.0 affects whole sprite, 0.35 keeps jitter localized.

falloff.name: Falloff
falloff.desc: Linear: broad shake. Smooth: softer edge blend. Exponential: concentrated center jitter.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5x5 mesh grid if none exists. No: skip if no mesh grid exists.

MeshPresetCombo.display-text: Apply mesh preset {0}, intensity {1}, center ({2}, {3}), angle {4}, auto mesh {5}
MeshPresetCombo.description: Apply a pre-configured combination of mesh effects tuned for specific game feel scenarios. Each preset blends 2–4 effects together. Intensity scales all effect strengths proportionally.

preset.name: Preset
preset.desc: Select a preset combination: Hit Impact (punch + jitter + bend for melee hits), Heavy Slam (shockwave + squash + ripple for large impacts), Sword Trail (impact trail + twist for slashing arcs), Wind Gust (directional bend + wave for environmental forces), Electric Stun (jitter + wobble + ripple for shock effects), Portal Spawn (twist + ripple + shockwave for magical spawns), UI Pop (punch + squash for UI interactions), Explosion Burst (strong shockwave + ripple + jitter), Jelly Bounce (wobble + vertical squash + gentle ripple), Whip Lash (directional bend + trail wave + jitter), Teleport Glitch (twist + jitter + small shockwave).

intensity.name: Intensity
intensity.desc: Multiplier for all effect strengths in this preset (0.5–2.0 typical). 1.0 is balanced. Lower values create subtle effects; higher values create exaggerated impacts.

centerX.name: Impact X
centerX.desc: Horizontal center point for effects (0=left, 0.5=center, 1=right). Ignored by effects that don't use center-based logic (e.g., Wind Gust).

centerY.name: Impact Y
centerY.desc: Vertical center point for effects (0=top, 0.5=center, 1=bottom). Ignored by effects that don't use center-based logic (e.g., Wind Gust).

angle.name: Angle (degrees)
angle.desc: Direction angle in degrees (0–360). Used by directional effects like Wind Gust and Sword Trail. Ignored by radial presets like Portal Spawn.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5×5 mesh grid if none exists (no setup required). No: skip the effect if no grid has been created yet with Create Grid.

MeshPunch.display-text: Punch at ({0}, {1}) strength {2}, radius {3}, falloff {4}, auto mesh {5}
MeshPunch.description: Blast all mesh vertices outward from a point, then spring back. Good for hit impacts, explosions, and shockwaves.

centerX.name: Impact X
centerX.desc: Horizontal impact point (0=left edge, 0.5=center, 1=right edge). To use a world-space hit position: (HitX - Sprite.BBoxLeft) / Sprite.Width.

centerY.name: Impact Y
centerY.desc: Vertical impact point (0=top edge, 0.5=center, 1=bottom edge). To use a world-space hit position: (HitY - Sprite.BBoxTop) / Sprite.Height.

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: Outward impulse per vertex. 0.2 is a light hit, 0.4 is a heavy impact, 0.6+ is explosive.

radius.name: Radius
radius.desc: How wide the blast spreads (normalized). 1.0 blasts the whole sprite. 0.3 creates a tight, localized dent at the impact point.

falloff.name: Falloff
falloff.desc: Linear: uniform strength across radius. Smooth: softer edges, more natural. Exponential: concentrated at center, sharp falloff.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5×5 mesh grid if none exists (no setup required). No: skip the effect if no grid has been created yet with Create Grid.

MeshRipple.display-text: Ripple at ({0}, {1}) strength {2}, wavelength {3}, decay {4}, auto mesh {5}
MeshRipple.description: Emit concentric rings of alternating push/pull from an origin point, like a stone dropped in water.

centerX.name: Origin X
centerX.desc: Horizontal wave origin (0=left edge, 0.5=center, 1=right edge). To use a world-space position: (ObjX - Sprite.BBoxLeft) / Sprite.Width.

centerY.name: Origin Y
centerY.desc: Vertical wave origin (0=top edge, 0.5=center, 1=bottom edge). Use 0.5 for a center splash or convert a world-space hit position.

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: Amplitude of each wave ring. 0.15 is a subtle ripple, 0.35 is a dramatic splash.

wavelength.name: Wavelength
wavelength.desc: Spacing between rings in normalized units. 0.25 gives ~4 rings across the sprite. 0.5 gives ~2 rings. Larger = fewer, wider rings.

decay.name: Decay
decay.desc: How quickly rings fade with distance from the origin. 0 = uniform rings across the whole sprite. 2 = rings fade quickly. 4+ = rings are very localized.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5×5 mesh grid if none exists (no setup required). No: skip the effect if no grid has been created yet with Create Grid.

MeshShockwave.display-text: Shockwave at ({0}, {1}) strength {2}, radius {3}, width {4}, auto mesh {5}
MeshShockwave.description: Emit a ring-shaped outward blast that peaks at a set distance from the origin. Unlike Punch, the center is unaffected — only the ring is hit. Good for bomb blasts and sonic booms.

centerX.name: Epicenter X
centerX.desc: Horizontal epicenter (0=left edge, 0.5=center, 1=right edge). To use a world-space position: (ObjX - Sprite.BBoxLeft) / Sprite.Width.

centerY.name: Epicenter Y
centerY.desc: Vertical epicenter (0=top edge, 0.5=center, 1=bottom edge). To use a world-space position: (ObjY - Sprite.BBoxTop) / Sprite.Height.

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: Outward impulse at the ring peak. 0.3 is a solid blast, 0.6 is explosive.

ringRadius.name: Ring Radius
ringRadius.desc: How far from the epicenter the ring sits (normalized). 0.0 puts the ring at the center (similar to Punch). 0.5 = ring is halfway to the sprite edge.

ringWidth.name: Ring Width
ringWidth.desc: Thickness of the ring on each side of the peak (normalized). 0.1 = tight sharp ring. 0.4 = wide, soft blast zone.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5×5 mesh grid if none exists (no setup required). No: skip the effect if no grid has been created yet with Create Grid.

MeshSquashStretch.list-name: Do Mesh Effect: Squash and stretch
MeshSquashStretch.display-text: Squash/stretch axis {0}, amount {1}, center ({2}, {3}), radius {4}, auto mesh {5}
MeshSquashStretch.description: Squeeze the sprite along one axis and bow it out along the other, then spring back. Classic animation squash/stretch principle.

axis.name: Axis
axis.desc: Vertical squashes top-to-bottom (use for landings). Horizontal squashes left-to-right (use for wall hits or wind-up).

amount.name: Amount
amount.desc: Impulse strength. 0.15-0.25 is a subtle bounce. 0.4+ is exaggerated cartoon feel. Negative reverses the squeeze direction.

centerX.name: Pivot X
centerX.desc: Horizontal pivot point (0=left edge, 0.5=center, 1=right edge). Use 0.5 for a symmetric squash.

centerY.name: Pivot Y
centerY.desc: Vertical pivot point (0=top edge, 0.5=center, 1=bottom edge). Use 1.0 for a ground landing (squashes from feet up). Use 0.0 for a ceiling hit.

radius.name: Radius
radius.desc: How far the effect spreads from the pivot (normalized). 1.0 deforms the whole sprite. Lower values create a localized bulge at the pivot point.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5×5 mesh grid if none exists (no setup required). No: skip the effect if no grid has been created yet with Create Grid.

MeshStopSway.description: Stop the continuous sway. The mesh vertices spring back to rest naturally — OnMeshSettled fires when they come to a stop.

MeshTwist.display-text: Twist at ({0}, {1}) strength {2}, radius {3}, falloff {4}, auto mesh {5}
MeshTwist.description: Swirl the mesh around a pivot in a rotational motion, then spring back. Good for portal effects, magic circles, spin attacks, and tornado impacts.

centerX.name: Pivot X
centerX.desc: Horizontal center of the swirl (0=left edge, 0.5=center, 1=right edge). Use 0.5 for a centered spin.

centerY.name: Pivot Y
centerY.desc: Vertical center of the swirl (0=top edge, 0.5=center, 1=bottom edge). Use 0.5 for a centered spin.

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: Rotational impulse. Positive = clockwise, negative = counter-clockwise. 0.2 is a gentle swirl, 0.5 is dramatic.

radius.name: Radius
radius.desc: How far from the pivot the twist reaches (normalized). 1.0 affects the whole sprite. 0.4 = localized core swirl only.

falloff.name: Falloff
falloff.desc: Linear: uniform spin across radius. Smooth: softer edges. Exponential: strongest at center, sharp drop-off.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5×5 mesh grid if none exists (no setup required). No: skip the effect if no grid has been created yet with Create Grid.

MeshWave.display-text: Wave angle {0}, strength {1}, wavelength {2}, auto mesh {3}
MeshWave.description: Push parallel bands of vertices in alternating directions, like a flag rippling in wind. Vertices move perpendicular to the wave travel direction.

angle.name: Angle
angle.desc: Direction the wave travels across the sprite in degrees. 0 = rightward (creates vertical bands, good for side-wind on a flag). 90 = downward (horizontal bands, good for vertical flutter).

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: Peak displacement per wave crest. 0.1 is a subtle flutter, 0.2 is a strong gust, 0.35+ is violent turbulence.

wavelength.name: Wavelength
wavelength.desc: Spacing between wave crests in normalized units. 0.5 = two crests across the sprite. 0.25 = four crests (tighter waves). 1.0 = one smooth S-curve across the whole sprite.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5×5 mesh grid if none exists (no setup required). No: skip the effect if no grid has been created yet with Create Grid.

MeshWobble.description: Shear the mesh in a direction — one side pushes one way, the opposite side pushes back. Good for hit reactions, wind gusts, and attack wind-ups.

angle.name: Angle
angle.desc: Direction of the shear in degrees. 0 = left/right shear (horizontal hit). 90 = up/down shear (vertical hit). Use angle() to match an attacker's direction.

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: How far the shear pushes. 0.1 is a subtle nudge, 0.2 is a solid hit, 0.35+ is dramatic. Negative values reverse the shear direction.

autoMesh.name: Auto Mesh
autoMesh.desc: Yes: automatically create a 5×5 mesh grid if none exists (no setup required). No: skip the effect if no grid has been created yet with Create Grid.

SetAutoGridResolution.description: Set the number of columns and rows used when Auto Mesh = Yes automatically creates a mesh. Higher values produce smoother, more detailed deformation at the cost of CPU. Default is 5×5. For subtle UI effects 4×4 is fine. For smooth squash/stretch on large sprites use 8×8 or higher.

cols.name: Columns
cols.desc: Number of mesh columns (2–32). More columns = smoother horizontal deformation. 5 is the default. Use 8–10 for smooth results on large sprites.

rows.name: Rows
rows.desc: Number of mesh rows (2–32). More rows = smoother vertical deformation. 5 is the default. Use 8–10 for smooth results on large sprites.
